question: What does Paul command in 2 Thessalonians 2:15 that supports the Catholic view of Tradition?

choices.A: 'Stand firm and hold fast to the traditions that you were taught, either by an oral statement or by a letter of ours' — explicitly endorsing both oral and written transmission
choices.B: 'Write everything down immediately so that nothing is lost' — commanding the creation of a complete written record
choices.C: 'Test all teachings against the Hebrew Scriptures alone' — establishing the OT as the sole norm
choices.D: 'Hold fast to nothing that was not spoken by the Lord himself' — limiting authority to the words of Jesus

teaching.title: 2 Thessalonians 2:15 — Oral and Written Tradition
teaching.body: In 2 Thessalonians 2:15, Paul explicitly commands holding fast to traditions (paradoseis) received 'either by an oral statement or by a letter.' This is one of the clearest NT affirmations that the apostolic deposit was transmitted both orally and in writing — not through writing alone. The word 'tradition' (paradosis) is the same used in 1 Corinthians 11:2 ('I praise you for remembering me in everything and for holding fast to the traditions just as I handed them on to you'). Catholic theology points to this as scriptural support for Sacred Tradition as a genuine channel of divine revelation.
